'''Neville Clinton Luhmann Jr.''' (March 10, 1943 – September 5, 2025) was an American physicist.

==Early life and career==
Luhmann was born in [[California]] on March 10, 1943, the son of Neville Sr. and Katherine Luhmann.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Neville C Luhmann Jr |url=https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/62308/records/267543564 |access-date=September 13, 2025 |publisher=1950 United States Federal Census |via=[[Ancestry.com]]}} {{Closed access}} {{Subscription required}}</ref> He attended the [[University of California, Berkeley]], earning his [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[engineering physics]] in 1966. He also attended the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in [[physics]] in 1972. After earning his degrees, he worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]].<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://everloved.com/life-of/neville-luhmann-jr/obituary/|title=Prof. Neville Clinton Luhmann Jr.|work=Ever Loved|access-date=September 13, 2025}}</ref><ref name="b">{{Cite web|url=https://ece.ucdavis.edu/news/memory-distinguished-professor-neville-c-luhmann-jr|title=In Memory of Distinguished Professor Neville C. Luhmann Jr.|first1=Yilun|last1=Zhu|first2=Zhi|last2=Ding|first3=Anh-Vu|last3=Pham|first4=Saif|last4=Islam|work=[[University of California, Davis]]|date=September 11, 2025|access-date=September 13, 2025}}</ref>

In 1987, Luhmann was elected as a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]], "for pioneering work in the development of innovative far-infared technology and diagnostics for fusion plasmas and for basic measurements in both laboratory and fusion plasmas".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners?q=luhmann&af=false|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=September 13, 2025}}</ref> He served as a professor in the department of [[Electrical engineering|electrical]] and [[Computer engineering|computer engineering]] at the [[University of California, Davis]] from 1993 to 2025. During his years as a professor, in 2003, he was named a [[distinguished professor]].<ref name="b" />

==Personal life and death==
In 1970, Luhmann married [[Janet Luhmann|Janet Gasior]], a fellow physicist.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-herald-news-graduate-students-engage/180982353/|title=Graduate Students Engaged: Janet Gasior, N. C. Luhmann To Wed in Spring|work=[[The Herald-News]]|location=[[Passaic, New Jersey]]|date=January 27, 1970|access-date=September 13, 2025|page=16|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> Their marriage lasted until Luhmann's death in 2025.<ref name="a" />

Luhmann died in [[Walnut Creek, California]] on September 5, 2025, at the age of 82.<ref name="a" />
